source.title: Information-Theoretic Progress Measures reveal Grokking is an Emergent Phase Transition
source.authors: Kenzo Clauw; S. Stramaglia; D. Marinazzo

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weight decay and initialization effects on delayed generalization in modular arithmetic, a setting outside the claim versions’ specified benchmarks and interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports text-described generalization outcomes for weight decay and initialization. Synergy and redundancy values are progress measures, not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7; cited prior work is not extracted as this study’s result.
record.test_reason: The study measures delayed generalization on modular addition and its relationship to weight decay, initialization, and neuronal synergy. None of its experiments tests V1–V8. A new task alone does not establish a T3 test of a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors interpret grokking as an emergent phase involving collective neuronal interactions, report that weight decay and initialization shape this phase, and propose early synergy peaks as predictors. They also present preliminary subnetwork evidence for a causal relationship, while acknowledging weak contrasts, clustering limitations, and the need for further experiments and statistical tests.
record.recipe_differences: Studies grokking on modular addition with a small fully connected network and information-theoretic progress measures; this differs from the claim versions’ specified natural-image and language benchmarks and interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with weight decay and initialization factor; weight decay 10 and 50 do not achieve grokking, and initialization factors 1 and 50 do not recover after a rapid synergy drop.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay and constrained-norm initialization affect delayed generalization on modular addition. Weight decay 10 and 50 prevent grokking in the reported runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay and initialization influence the timing and occurrence of grokking in small modular-addition networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Early synergy peaks accompany successful grokking conditions. Isolated synergistic subnetworks show similar or earlier generalization, although their contrast with inverse subnetworks is sometimes small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-order neuronal synergy may provide a progress measure for grokking; its predictive and causal interpretation needs further validation.

record.problems: The authors call the work preliminary and identify the simplicity of the model and benchmark, difficulty scaling O-Information, and limitations of agglomerative clustering. They also state that further experiments and statistical tests are needed to verify the synergy prediction hypothesis.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted. Figures provide plotted train/test accuracy, but exact values are not stated in the text, so values are recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting with natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or optimizer-tuning comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No dropout experiment; synergistic dropout is proposed as future work.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, sharpness–generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or comparison with random-example removal.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row measures an outcome outside those versions. This does not negate the paper's reported grokking outcomes. No missing result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Uses AdamW only; does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Uses full-batch optimization; does not compare batch sizes.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking of generalization gaps with norm- or margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular addition with weight decay 0.1.

rows.check: Delayed generalization is reported, but it measures no listed version. Weight decay 0.1 agrees with Figure 1 and Section 5.1; Section 4 inconsistently says 0.01. Exact accuracy values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
